decision: DIFFERS -> W1: author the page's figure. iastate_ext growing-kohlrabi states "After thinning, kohlrabi seedlings should be spaced 6-8 inches apart within the row." -> in_row [6,8]; "When planting kohlrabi in the garden, sow seeds in rows spaced 18 to 24 inches apart." -> row [18,24]. Today's [6,9] has no page for 9 (USU 6 / rows 12; UMN 4; VCE 4-6; NMSU 3-6; VH021 3-5). Twelve prose strings restating 6-9 are re-authored to 6-8; container notes (about 6 in) and per-row fertilizer rates agree.

edits.new: Thin to 6 to 8 inches, grow in full sun, and go easy on nitrogen late in the crop.

edits.new: The plant grew plenty of leaves but never formed a real bulb. This usually comes from plants set too close together, too much shade, or a lot of nitrogen late on, all of which push leafy growth over the bulb. Next time, thin to 6 to 8 inches, grow in full sun, and keep feeding modest and even.

edits.new: The plant made foliage but no usable swollen stem. The usual causes are crowding, insufficient light, or excess late nitrogen, each favoring leaves over the bulb. Next time thin to 6 to 8 inches, site in full sun, and keep nitrogen modest and front-loaded so the plant transitions to bulbing.

edits.new: Thin direct-sown seedlings to about 6 to 8 inches apart. Before planting transplants outside, harden them off over about a week, and avoid setting them out into a long cold snap.
edits.reason: restates the moved in-row figure (ISU: 6-8 in)

edits.new: Thin to 6 to 8 inches; harden off transplants over 7 to 10 days and avoid exposing young plants to a prolonged cold spell, which vernalizes them and triggers bolting.
edits.reason: restates the moved in-row figure (ISU: 6-8 in)

edits.new: You can sow kohlrabi seeds right in the garden or start with young plants. For direct sowing, plant the seeds about a quarter to half an inch deep once the soil can be worked, then thin the seedlings to about 6 to 8 inches apart. For transplants, start seeds indoors about a month before planting out, and set them in the garden a week or two before the last frost. Let homegrown seedlings get used to the outdoors over a week before planting. Sow again in mid-summer for a fall crop.
edits.reason: restates the moved in-row figure (ISU: 6-8 in)

edits.new: Kohlrabi is grown both ways. Direct sowing is simple and common since the crop is fast: sow 1/4 to 1/2 inch deep once the soil is workable and thin to 6 to 8 inches apart. For an earlier or more uniform crop, start transplants indoors about 4 to 5 weeks before set-out and plant them out 1 to 2 weeks before the last frost, since young plants take light frost. Avoid exposing young plants to a long cold spell (more than about a week of nights below roughly 45 to 50°F), which can trigger bolting. Sow the fall crop in mid-summer. Harden transplants off over 7 to 10 days.
edits.reason: restates the moved in-row figure (ISU: 6-8 in)

edits.new: When the seedlings have a few real leaves, thin them so each plant has about 6 to 8 inches of room. Snip the extras off at the soil instead of pulling, so you don't disturb the ones you keep. Crowded kohlrabi makes small, poor bulbs.
edits.reason: restates the moved in-row figure (ISU: 6-8 in)

edits.new: Thin direct-sown kohlrabi to 6 to 8 inches apart once seedlings have 2 to 3 true leaves, snipping rather than pulling to avoid disturbing the keepers. Crowded plants compete for moisture and make small, misshapen bulbs, and crowding stress can also push them woody.
edits.reason: restates the moved in-row figure (ISU: 6-8 in)

edits.new: Thin the seedlings to about 6 to 8 inches apart so each one has room to form a good bulb.
edits.reason: restates the moved in-row figure (ISU: 6-8 in)

edits.new: Thin to 6 to 8 inches apart; crowded plants make small, misshapen bulbs and compete for moisture.

edits.new: Spacing and succession: yield over the season comes from spacing at 6 to 8 inches and sowing in small batches every 2 to 3 weeks.
